name: Issue resolution desk
description: A config-driven, repo-agnostic issue-resolution desk. A GitHub issue (bound to a task by the github sync) is picked up by an implementer Claude Code agent that runs in the platform's own ephemeral sandbox on the user's BYO Claude credentials: it derives the repo from the issue, clones it, fixes the issue on a tale/<id> branch, runs the project's OWN tests to verify, commits, pushes (broker-injected github token + the in-image credential helper, private repos included), opens a pull request, and then WAITS for the project's CI to pass green — fixing failures and re-pushing until it does. The sandbox step is durable: it transparently spans the 10-minute Convex action ceiling (segmenting into re-attached windows), so a 40-50 minute CI run never times the step out, with no separate CI-poll step. A separate reviewer agent fetches the PR, re-runs the tests, confirms CI is green, and posts review comments. A toolless LLM judge then reads the review and decides merge-readiness: if yes, the task parks at In review and the workflow ends (the human merges); if no, it loops back to the implementer with the review feedback, repeating until the judge approves — or until the rework loop hits a configurable cap (config.variables.maxReworkLoops, default 3, adjustable per deployment), after which the desk stops looping, comments on the task, and parks it at In review for a human to take over. Cross-step state lives on the git branch + PR (plus a reworkCount loop counter in workflow variables); the per-step sandboxes are stateless. Every step carries ui/role annotations so the generic operator workspace renders it with no per-vertical UI code.

steps.name: Implementer resolves the issue & opens/updates the PR

config.description: A sandbox step always returns the success port; the real verdict is in output.data.ok. Stop if the implementer failed to push a verified fix + PR.

parameters.body: [automated] The implementer could not resolve this issue: {{steps.implement.output.data.error || steps.implement.output.data.summary || 'no output'}} — returned to To do.

steps.name: Reviewer re-tests & comments on the PR

run.instructions: Review the implementer's fix for '{{input.task.title}}' (#{{input.issueNumber}}) at {{input.task.externalUrl}} on branch `tale/{{input.task._id}}`. Git is authenticated ($GITHUB_TOKEN + helper). SET UP ONCE: (1) derive the repo URL from the issue URL and `cd /user/workspace && git clone <repo> repo && cd repo`; (2) `git fetch origin tale/{{input.task._id}} && git checkout tale/{{input.task._id}}`; (3) run the project's OWN tests a single time here, so your review subagents don't each re-run the suite. THEN REVIEW BY YOUR FULL METHOD — do NOT collapse this into one linear sweep: run ROUND 1 (breadth) by dispatching the parallel per-dimension review subagents your system instructions define, then ROUND 2 (confirmation) independently re-verifying every finding you would block the merge on. As part of the bar, confirm the PR's CI with `gh pr checks tale/{{input.task._id}}` — red OR still-pending CI is a BLOCKING problem you must call out. REPORT: post your review as comments on the pull request (`gh pr review` / `gh pr comment`, or the GitHub REST API with $GITHUB_TOKEN) — do NOT change or push code, the implementer fixes. MANDATORY: write your findings to /user/output/summary.md (absolute path): state the CI state (which checks passed/failed) and clearly whether the change is ready to merge or what specifically must be fixed.

config.name: merge-judge
config.systemPrompt: You are a strict merge gate for a code-review desk. You are given ONLY the reviewer's written summary of a proposed fix. Decide whether it is ready to merge: approve only when the reviewer reports no blocking problems and the tests pass. You have no tools and must judge solely from the summary. Reply with EXACTLY one lowercase word and nothing else: yes (ready to merge) or no (needs more work).

config.description: The judge replies with a bare yes/no (trimmed); jexl `in` does substring, and a 'no' can never contain 'yes', so this never false-approves. If yes, park for human merge; otherwise route through the rework counter, which loops back to the implementer with the review feedback until the configurable cap is reached.

Bounds the review -> implement rework loop. reworkCount (workflow variables) counts how many times the reviewer has sent the change back; allow up to config.variables.maxReworkLoops reworks (default 3, adjustable per deployment). While within budget, loop back to the implementer with the latest feedback; once exhausted, escalate to a human instead of looping until the workflow timeout.

steps.name: Rework limit reached — escalate to a human

parameters.body: [automated] The desk reached its rework limit ({{config.maxReworkLoops}} loops) without the reviewer approving the change. The pull request is left open with the latest attempt and the review feedback — a human should take it over from here. Moving to In review.
